references.text: The account of Elijah being sent to the widow in Zarephath in Sidon during the famine. Jesus refers directly to this event in 1 Kings to show that God sent the prophet to a Gentile widow, not to any of the widows in Israel.
The background to the famine that struck Israel in Elijah's time, when the sky was shut up for three years and six months, as Jesus has just mentioned in the previous verse.
The description of the great famine in Samaria during Elijah's time, which forms the context for Elijah being sent to Zarephath.
The preceding verse that provides the context: there were many widows in Israel in Elijah's days when the sky was shut up for three years and six months and a great famine came over all the land.
The following verse continues Jesus' point with a parallel example: there were many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, but none of them were cleansed, only Naaman the Syrian.
Jesus' opening statement that no prophet is accepted in his hometown, which serves as the basis for the examples of Elijah and Elisha.
Jesus mentions Sidon in connection with judgment and repentance among Gentiles, which is thematically linked to God's blessing of Gentiles like the widow in Zarephath in the region of Sidon.
Jesus meets a Canaanite woman from the region of Tyre and Sidon and commends her faith—a parallel to God's care for Gentiles in the Sidon area, such as the widow in Zarephath.
